newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk Vakif Leasing aims 86pct volume rise.
newsitem.headline: Turk Vakif Leasing aims 86pct volume rise.

text.p: Turkish leasing firm Vakif Finansal Kiralama A.S. is targeting an increase in its 1997 turnover of 86 percent to 32 trillion lira, a senior company official said.
"Our total business volume in 1996 was 17.2 trillion lira and we aim to raise it to 32 trillion lira this year," Ertugrul Yurdacan, general manager of the company, told Reuters.
The company reported 1.57 trillion lira of net profits in 1996, up 655 percent from 208.3 billion lira a year ago. Its capital stands at 1.2 trillion lira.
Company shares opened at 6,600 lira on the Istanbul Stock Exchange on Tuesday, up from Monday's 6,400 lira close.
Yurdacan said 1996 was a good year for the Turkish leasing sector and both the number of new companies and overall turnover increased.
"We focused more on industries and companies' organisational investments (last year). We secured foreign financing and raised our borrowing maturities to five years from two," said Yurdacan.
He added that they preferred to borrow from eximbanks in Germany, France, Belgium, the Netherlands and Austria.
Yurdacan said Vakif was the first leasing firm to invest in Turkey's energy sector last year and would continue similar investment this year.
The main shareholders of the company are state-owned Vakifbank with a 59.48 percent stake and the bank's insurance joint-venture Gunes Sigorta A.S. with 15.06 percent.
Vakif Leasing took a 25 percent share in Vakifbank's newly established factoring firm Vakif Factoring which has a 250 billion lira capital and will begin operations this year.
